title: Lighthouse priority catalog and cross-team commitment slate
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: build a single source-of-truth 'Lighthouse Priority Catalog' that maps company-level OKRs to a concise slate of cross-team initiatives (the Commitment Slate). The catalog will be used by execs, PMs, and engineering leads to make trade-offs each quarter, trigger resourcing decisions (dedicated vs. hosted), and power the roadmap UI and stakeholder rollup.

Scope: a machine-readable catalog + human-friendly views: 1) canonical OKR -> initiative linkage with rationale and owner, 2) commitment SLAs (commitment level, confidence, essential milestones), 3) impact and effort estimates, 4) cross-team dependency graph and escalation path, 5) change-log and gating runbook for mid-cycle reprioritization.

Out-of-scope: automated funding/reallocation tooling, enforcement of team-level sprint boards. We will provide recommendations and triggers but not automated org changes in this phase.

Why now: multiple SLAs and capacity conflicts surfaced during last two quarters (see PM-314159 and PM-75291). Teams are spending too much time reconciling priorities, which increases delivery variability. The catalog reduces coordination tax and improves predictability for Dedicated and Private sales commitments.

Stakeholders: Ava Martinez (PM lead), Liam Chen (release owner), Priya Nair (Product Ops), Daniel Kim (APIs lead), Sophia Gomez (Engineering manager - Runtime), Kate O'Neill (Design lead), Customer Success and Sales for enterprise input.

Deliverables: 1) CSV/JSON canonical catalog + change log, 2) Confluence primer and decision rubric, 3) lightweight UI mockups for Console roadmap integration, 4) handoff playbook for quarterly roll and mid-cycle reprioritization, 5) short pilot with two cross-functional initiatives (runtime batching and Dedicated autoscale policy).

Success metrics: reduce cross-team coordination incidents by 40% (measured via Ops tickets), 30% faster decision time for cross-team escalations, and 90% coverage for company OKRs mapped to initiatives prior to Q2 planning.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Each company-level OKR has at least one mapped initiative and named owner in the catalog.
2) Catalog is available as JSON and as a Confluence page with decision rubric.
3) Two pilot initiatives completed the Commitment Slate flow and used it to drive resource decisions.
4) Playbook for mid-cycle changes published and promoted to PM/Eng leads.
5) At least one Console roadmap mock implemented as a prototype and demoed to execs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: teams will treat the slate as prescriptive rather than a coordination tool. Mitigation: include explicit commitment levels and confidence bands; require engineering sign-off for any resource reassignments.

Risk: keeping the catalog up-to-date will fall to a single person. Mitigation: design the catalog for lightweight ownership (owners per initiative + monthly health ping) and integrate with existing roadmap exports.
Risk: overlap with existing OKR artifacts. Mitigation: align with Strategy Ops and archive duplicate docs during the pilot.
